title: pvCesium3DTilesReader
body:
## pvCesium3DTilesReader

Reads a Cesium 3D Tiles tileset (the tileset .json file and the glTF, GLB or B3DM tiles it references) into a partitioned dataset collection with one partitioned dataset per tile. Coordinates stay in the tileset's Cartesian frame, typically Earth-centred metres for georeferenced city or terrain models. Use it to bring photogrammetry or city meshes into a pipeline; Level chooses how deep in the tile tree to read.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- ParaView 5.13.3 starts from Level 0, the root (coarsest) tiles; increase Level for more detail, at the cost of reading many more tiles.
- Earth-centred coordinates are millions of metres from the origin; translate the data before combining it with local-coordinate models.
- Schemaxis generates this reader binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check with a sample file of this format.

Native constructor: `Cesium3DTilesReader`. Identity: `sources/Cesium3DTiles Reader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FileName` | Specify file name of the Cesium3DTiles tileset to read. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Level` | Level in the tree we read tiles from. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvCesium3DTilesReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
